name: Swadesh 215 (1955)
description: A broad foundational vocabulary for basic words across everyday domains.
attribution: List, Johann Mattis & Tjuka, Annika & Blum, Frederic & Kučerová, Alžběta & Ugarte, Carlos Barrientos & Rzymski, Christoph & Greenhill, Simon & Forkel, Robert (eds.) 2025. Concepticon v3.4.0. A Resource for the Linking of Concept Lists. Leipzig: Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology. https://concepticon.clld.org

concepts.definition: The totality of.
Used to connect two homogeneous words or phrases.

Any living organism characterized by voluntary movement, the possession of cells with noncellulose cell walls and specialized sense organs enabling rapid response to stimuli, and the ingestion of complex organic substances such as plants and other animals.
The incombustible matter remaining after a substance has been incinerated.
To be in a particular place or location.
The rear of body, especially the part between the neck and the end of the spine and opposite the chest and belly.
Not good; unfavorable; negative.
The exterior covering of the trunk and branches of a tree.
Conjunction initiating a causal phrase.
The lower part of the front of the torso (or a comparable part of an animal), confined by the upper side by the midriff and the lowerside by the pelvis. Contains the intestines.
A soft fruit which develops from a superior ovary and contains seeds not encased in pits.
Of a great size.
Any of the bipedal, warm-blooded vertebrates that lay eggs having wings which, for most species, enables them to fly.
Clamping the teeth hard on something.
Dark and colourless; not reflecting visible light.
A fluid connective tissue consisting of the plasma and cells that circulate in the blood vessels.
(Of the wind or a current of air) To move.
Any of the components of an endoskeleton, consisting mainly of calcium phosphate, collagen and cells.
To repeatedly draw air into, and expel it from, the lungs, in order to extract oxygen from it and excrete waste products.
A male person who has the same parents as another person.
To put fire on something or to be on fire.
A young human or the descendant of a human.
All coverings designed to be worn on a person's body.
Suspensions of minute water droplets or ice crystals produced by the condensation of water vapour.
Having a low temperature.
To move toward or to reach either the speaker, the person spoken to, or the subject of the speaker's narrative.
To prepare a meal or a single dish.
To determine the amount of something or to enumerate the digits of one's numeral system.
To shed tears due to the impact of an emotion.
To perform an incision (for example, with a knife).
To move with rhythmic steps or movements, especially in time to music.
The period between sunrise and sunset where one enjoys daylight.
To cease to live.
To move earth, rocks, etc. out of the way, usually to create a hole.
Covered with or containing unpleasant substances such as dirt or grime.
A common four-legged animal, especially kept by people as a pet or to hunt or guard things.
To consume a liquid through the mouth.
(Almost) free from liquid or moisture.
Having a thick edge or point, as an instrument; not sharp.
Any kind of solid material divided in particles of very small size.
The organ of hearing, consisting of the pinna, auditory canal, eardrum, malleus, incus, stapes and cochlea.
The soft and loose material forming a great part of the Earth surface.
To consume something solid or semi-solid (usually food) by putting it into the mouth and eventually swallowing it.
Egg (either fertilized or not) from domesticated birds, most commonly hens, seen as food.
The natural number eight (8).
The organ that is sensitive to light, which it converts to electrical signals passed to the brain, by which means animals and humans see.
To descend in free fall due to the effect of gravity.
Having a large intervening distance with regard to something.
Esters of three fatty acid chains and the alcohol glycerol which form a semi-solid substance in room temperature and occur in animals and plants.
A male parent.
To be scared of; to have an uncontrollable emotion of anxiety about something that causes a scared reaction or frightening impression.
A branching, hair-like structure that grows on the skin of birds and protects them against coldness and water and allows their wings to create lift.
More than one, but not as many as usual or as expected.
To be involved in a physical confrontation.
The state of combustion in which inflammable material burns, producing heat, flames and often smoke.
A cold-blooded vertebrate animal that lives in water that moves with the help of fins and breathes using gills (Pisces).
The natural number five (5).
Of an object or substance, to be supported by a liquid of greater density than the object so as that part of the object or substance remains above the surface. [WK:float]
To move as a fluid from one position to another (e.g. of water or of people).
The reproductive structure of angiosperm plants, consisting of stamens and carpels surrounded by petals and sepals all borne on the receptacle.
To move autonomously through the air, without any part of the object or object's enclosure touching anything attached to the ground.
Water droplets or, rarely, ice crystals suspended in the air in sufficient concentration to reduce visibility appreciably.
The part of a human’s body below the ankle that is used in order to stand and walk.
The natural number four (4).
To reach a chemically solid state, by the process of cooling.
To transfer the possession or holding (of an object) to another person.
Having desired or positive qualities.

A very large and widespread family of Monocotyledoneae, with more than 10.000 species, most of which are herbaceous, but a few are woody. The stems are jointed, the long, narrow leaves originating at the nodes. The flowers are inconspicuous, with a much reduced perianth, and are wind-pollinated or cleistogamous.

Having green as its colour; having the hue of that portion of the visible spectrum lying between yellow and blue, evoked in the human observer by radiant energy with wavelengths of approximately 490 to 570 nanometers.
The internal organs of an animal or human.
The hair on humans, usually on the head but also including the hair on the body.
That part of the fore limb below the forearm or wrist in primates (including humans).
A male other; the male previously mentioned; himself.  3rd person singular masculine subject pronoun.
The part of the body of an animal or human which contains the brain, mouth and main sense organs.
To perceive sound with the ear, without necessarily paying attention to it.
A muscular organ that pumps blood through the body.
At this place.
To hit against with a sharp blow or to impel, usually with a hand or weapon or to be forcefully or suddenly contacting, e.g. a tree falling down and hitting the ground.
To grasp or grip (particularly with the hand) so that the object does not end up at the surface below.
In what way?
The natural number one hundred (100).
To chase down prey and (usually) kill it.
The male partner in a marriage.
The speaker or writer referring to himself or herself alone.
The dense substance formed by the freezing of water to the solid state; it commonly occurs in the form of hexagonal crystals.
[The introduction of a condition or decision.]
Contained or encased by something.
To put to death; to end a life.
To be sure about something or be acquainted with something.
An enclosed body of water, usually but not necessarily fresh water, from which the sea is excluded.

To express pleasure, mirth or derision by peculiar movement of the muscles of the face, particularly of the mouth, causing a lighting up of the face and eyes, and usually accompanied by the emission of explosive or chuckling sounds from the chest and throat.
The main organ of photosynthesis and transpiration in higher plants, usually consisting of a flat green blade attached to the stem directly or by a stalk.
Something that is on the left side relative to another object.
The limb of an animal (including humans) that extends from the groin to the ankle.
To rest in a horizontal, static position, usually on another surface.
To be alive; to have a life.
A large organ in the body that stores and metabolizes nutrients, destroys toxins and produces bile. Responsible for thousands of biochemical reactions.
Having much distance from one terminating point on an object or an area to another terminating point.
A small wingless parasitic insect of the order Phthiraptera that lives on humans, other mammals and birds.
An adult human member of the sex that begets young by fertilizing ova.
An indefinite large number of.
Either referring to the soft substance of the body of living things (flesh), or to the soft substance in animals as an important source of food for humans.
A woman who has at least one child.
A feature of the earth's surface that rises high above the base and has generally steep slopes and a relatively small summit area.
Opening in the lower half of a human face which is used for food ingestion and articulation.
Any word or phrase which designates a particular person, place, class or thing.
(Of a path, cave etc.) having a small width.
Not far distant in time or space or degree or circumstances.
The part of the body (found in some animals, including humans) that connects the head and the trunk.
Recently made, created or begun.
The period between sunset and sunrise, when a location faces far away from the sun, thus when the sky is dark.
The natural number nine (9).
The organ of the face used to breath and smell.
Negates the meaning of the modified verb or adjective.
Having lived or existed for a relatively long period of time.
The natural number one (1).
The rest of a group of.
A human being.
To act in a manner such that one has fun; to engage in playful activities expressly for the purpose of recreation.
To apply a force to (an object), in order that it moves towards the origin of the force that was applied.
To apply a force to (an object), in order that it moves away from the origin of the force that was applied.
The process by which water falls from the clouds or the water that falls from the clouds.
Having red as its colour.
Something that is on the right side relative to another object.
To be in accordance with expectations.
A stream of water which flows in a channel from high ground to low ground and ultimately to a lake or the sea, except in a desert area where it may dwindle away to nothing.
A long piece of hard ground that people can drive along from one place to another.
The absorbing and anchoring organ of a vascular plant; it bears neither leaves nor flowers and is usually subterranean.
Thick, strong string made of several strands that have been twisted together.
Having changed its colour, smell or composition (partially or completely), due to being attacked and decomposed by microorganisms (relating to organic matter).
To move one's hand or an object over a surface or other object (maintaining constant contact and applying moderate pressure).
A condiment (NaCl - Sodium Chloride) used to add to or enhance the flavour of food (commonly with pepper).

A loose material consisting of small mineral particles, or rock and mineral particles, distinguishable by the naked eye; grains vary from almost spherical to angular, with a diameter range from 1/16 to 2 millimeters.
To rub or scrape (a part of the body) with a sharp object (e.g. to relieve an itching).
A body of salt water that is smaller than an ocean and generally in proximity to a continent.
To perceive [images] with the eye, without necessarily paying attention to them.
A mature fertilized plant ovule, consisting of an embryo and its food store surrounded by a protective seed coat (testa).
The natural number seven (7).
To pass thread repeatedly through fabric or a material, using a needle, in order to join two or more parts or to make a pattern or motif.
Having the ability to cut easily.
To fire a shot from a firearm, bow or other weapon.
Small in length by comparison.
To produce harmonious sounds with one's voice.
A female person who has the same parents as another person.
To be in a position with the upper body upright and the legs resting.
The natural number six (6).

The tissue forming the outer covering of the vertebrate body: it consists of two layers, the outermost of which may be covered with hair, scales, feathers, etc. It is mainly protective and sensory in function.
The part of the earth's atmosphere and space outside it that is visible from earth's surface. During the day it is perceived as blue, and at night as black.
To rest in a state of decreased consciousness and reduced metabolism.
Not large or big; small in size.
Perceive or emit odour.
An aerosol, consisting of visible particles and gases, produced by the incomplete burning of carbon-based materials, such as wood and fossil fuels.
Not rough; having a surface texture that lacks friction.
Any reptile of the suborder Serpentes, typically having a scaly cylindrical limbless body, fused eyelids, and a jaw modified for swallowing large prey.
The most common form of frozen precipitation, usually flakes or starlike crystals, matted ice needles, or combinations, and often rime-coated.
An unspecified quantity or number of.
To communicate by the use of words.
a long, stabbing weapon for thrusting or throwing, consisting of a wooden shaft to which a sharp-pointed head, as of iron or steel, is attached.
To forcefully evacuate saliva from the mouth.
To divide fully or partly along a more or less straight line.
To apply pressure to something from two or more sides at once.
To perforate the surface of something with a pointed tool or weapon.
To be upright in an erect position, supported by the feet.
A luminous celestial body that is made from gases (particularly hydrogen and helium) and forms the shape of a sphere.
A long, thin piece of wood, mainly left in the shape in which it grew, that does not bend.
A general term for rock that is used in construction, either crushed for use as aggregate or cut into shaped blocks as dimension stone.
Not crooked or bent; having a constant direction throughout its length.
To draw in a substance by creating a practical vacuum in the mouth, and as a result a difference in pressure.
The particular star at the centre of our solar system, from which the Earth gets light and heat.
To grow larger in volume.
To move through the water, without touching the bottom.
The appendage of an animal that is attached to its posterior and near the anus.
The natural number ten (10).
The indicated object, item, etc. distant from the speaker.
In a not completely determined place which is not here.
The third person plural of the personal pronoun that designates more than one person or animal, thing or idea which have already been mentioned previously.
Relatively large distance from one surface to the opposite in its smallest solid dimension.
Being narrow or carrying a small amount of fat.
Use ones mental power to form ideas or having used ones mental power to form ideas of conviction or belief.
The indicated object, item, etc. close to the speaker.
The person addressed.
The natural number three (3).
To cause (an object) to move rapidly through the air, with the force of the hand or arm.
To establish connection between two or more things.

The flexible muscular organ in the mouth that is used to move food around, for tasting and that is moved into various positions to modify the flow of air from the lungs in order to produce different sounds.
A hard, calcareous structure present in the mouth of many vertebrate animals (including humans), generally used for eating.
Any large woody perennial plant with a distinct trunk giving rise to branches or leaves at some distance from the ground.
To change the direction of movement or the direction in which something is facing.
The natural number twenty (20).
The natural number two (2).
To regurgitate the contents of the stomach.
To move from one place to another by moving legs alternately, so that at least one foot is in contact with the floor or surface at any one time.
Having a higher temperature than normal.
To remove dirt and grime from an object, using water (usually with soap).
Common liquid (H₂O) which forms rain, rivers, the sea, etc., and which makes up a large part of the bodies of organisms.
The speaker or writer and at least one other person.
Covered with or impregnated with liquid.
Which thing.
At what time?
At what place?
Bright and colourless; reflecting equal quantities of all frequencies of visible light.
What person or people; which person or people.
Having a long distance or area between two points, especially horizontally.
The female partner in a marriage.
The motion of air relative to the earth's surface; usually means horizontal air motion, as distinguished from vertical motion.
The appendage of an animal's (bird, bat, insect) body that enables it to fly in the air.
To move an object or utensil over a surface or other object while maintaining contact, in order that a substance be removed from its surface.
In the company of.
An adult human member of the sex that produces ova and bears young.
A vegetation community dominated by trees and other woody shrubs, growing close enough together that the tree tops touch or overlap, creating various degrees of shade on the forest floor.
To do a specific task by employing physical or mental powers.
A generally tubular invertebrate of the annelid phylum.
The group of persons addressed.
The time it takes the Earth to complete one revolution of the Sun (between 365.24 and 365.26 days depending on the point of reference).
Having the colour of a yolk, a lemon or gold.
